One of the worst things about reddit is that users started sorting themselves into some kind of pointless hierarchy based upon their vote scores. This led to all kinds of miniature reddit "celebrities" who then inevitably abused the status to sell out and shill products which ultimately tied money to their activity on reddit and led to cliques, cults and fighting resulting in reddit today.

Votes should be invisible, people shouldn't be able to tabulate their scores to "game" the system and top ranked posts in discussions should be shuffled randomly among the top ten in a discussion so that no one can deduce a pattern to see who's a "celebrity" and so they can't form a pecking-order.

I kind of like this but I think at the same time people need to know how their post has done. That way they can learn what is and isn't wanted in their particular subverse. It's annoying when people whore themselves for points and abuse an imaginary position based on imaginary points, but I think the upvoat/downvoat system should stay and is a necessary thing.

You can upvote and downvote, I just propose that the numbers are invisible to users while the votes will let their comments rise or fall. So you can get a "feeling" for how well your comment does but the feeling won't be accurate enough to award any ego points (the lack of which will drive away people who just want the attention and validation, also it keeps people from shaping their comments and mindsets for the most points). Especially since if the top spot for comments are regularly shuffled among ten nobody will be able to determine who's "popular" and form echo chambers. If people want a real discussion then they should read all of the comments instead of just the #1 most generally inoffensive and agreed with.

That way people don't devolve into echo boxes which devolve into cults.
